en.title: Matt Groening Teases The Simpsons: Hit & Run Return, Then Backtracks
en.summary: A seemingly accidental hint from Simpsons creator Matt Groening about The Simpsons: Hit & Run returning has ignited fan hopes. However, a quick interjection from showrunner Matt Selman has cast doubt on the specifics, leaving fans scrambling for clarity.
en.body:
For over two decades, fans have yearned for a return to the chaotic, open-world streets of Springfield in **The Simpsons: Hit & Run**. Now, a cryptic comment from the show's creator, **Matt Groening**, has sent ripples of excitement through the gaming community, suggesting the classic 2003 title might be making a comeback.

During a panel at the recent D23 fan event in 2026, Groening was reportedly asked about the possibility of a new **Hit & Run** game. His response, as relayed by IGN and Empire, seemed to confirm a revival. "I think the original game is coming back in some form," Groening stated. This statement alone was enough to set social media ablaze, with many interpreting it as a direct hint towards a remaster or remake of the beloved PlayStation 2, GameCube, and Xbox title. The game, developed by Radical Entertainment and published by Vivendi Games, remains a fan favorite for its surprisingly robust gameplay that blended Grand Theft Auto's open-world mechanics with the iconic humor and characters of The Simpsons.

However, the elation was short-lived. Almost immediately after Groening's comment, current **The Simpsons** showrunner **Matt Selman** stepped in, adding a rather dampening "...or not." This quick retraction has left the status of any potential **Hit & Run** revival in a state of considerable uncertainty. Was this a premature announcement from Groening, or did Selman perhaps overstep in shutting down the possibility? Without further clarification, it's impossible to say, but the creator's initial tease has undeniably reignited conversations about this cherished game.

## The Internet Reacts to the Springfield Shuffle

The mere mention of **The Simpsons: Hit & Run** returning, even with the subsequent "or not," was enough to send fans into a frenzy. For years, the game has been a consistent topic of wishlists and fan campaigns, with many hoping for a modern iteration that would bring its unique brand of vehicular mayhem and mission-based gameplay to current-generation consoles. The hope is that if a revival does occur, it will be a faithful remaster or a full remake, rather than a reboot that might stray too far from the original's beloved formula. The ambiguity now surrounding Groening's comment means fans are left eagerly awaiting any concrete news, with expectations tempered but hope still very much alive.

## What's Next for Hit & Run?

At present, details remain exceptionally scarce. The contradictory statements from Groening and Selman mean that any official confirmation of a **The Simpsons: Hit & Run** revival is still pending. Fans should keep a close eye on official **The Simpsons** channels and game developer announcements for any future updates, but for now, the future of the game remains as hazy as a Springfield smog day.

content_raw: The Simpsons: Hit & Run "is coming back in some form," according to series creator Matt Groening. Yes, at least as far as the mind behind Springfield and the Simpson family is concerned, Vivendi Games and Radical Entertainment's classic 2000s video game spinoff will finally soon let players get behind the wheel again. He shared his comments during a The Simpsons panel at Disney fan event D23 2026, but it sounds like, maybe, he should have pumped the brakes when it came to any announcements for The Simpsons: Hit & Run. "I think the original game is coming back in some form," Groening said (via Empire ). Just as Groening let it slip that the Grand Theft Auto-inspired game was coming back, current series showrunner Matt Selman stepped in, saying, "…or not." Whoops. So, is this a premature announcement, or does Groening have it all wrong? It's difficult to say for now, but when the creator of the franchise the game is based on says The Simpsons: Hit & Run is making some sort of return, it's hard not to raise an eyebrow. The internet felt the same, as social media feeds quickly filled up with joy as it seemed a 23-year drought without the game could soon come to an end. Groening's mentioning of "the original game" suggests players might want to expect something more like a remaster or remake and not a sequel or reboot. It's hard to know exactly what's coming without something a little more concrete, sadly, so until a more official announcement arrives, it's probably best to keep expectations in check. What a classic! Hopefully it's a remake/remaster for next gen! pic.twitter.com/zZPAWVhNTv — Andre Saint-Albin (@AndreSaintAlbin) August 14, 2026 The Simpsons: Hit & Run originally launched for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and original Xbox in 2003, and all these years later, it remains not only as one of the standout games of the generation but one of the more memorable licensed games of all time. With Springfield re-imagined without losing the show's iconic style, GTA-like gameplay, and the series' iconic sense of humor, it's easy to see why fans have clamored to see it return for all these years. IGN gave the game an 8.1/10 review . We said at the time that, while it's not a perfect game overall, it's still "undeniably the perfect game for Simpsons fans." Some of the original The Simpsons: Hit & Run developers said they were shocked it had never made a comeback during an interview with MinnMax in 2023. The years have gone by with few updates, but in March of this year, Selman teased that fans should "never say never." For now, unfortunately, a The Simpsons: Hit & Run remaster/remake has not been officially announced. Until there is hopefully more to share, you can read about how the rebirth of Radical Entertainment got fans excited earlier this year . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN.
